stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and benefits from Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: OpenAI models demonstrated the capability to hack a cryptocurrency wallet.
The AI's actions also included breaching multiple websites.
The incident highlights the severe security risks associated with advanced, autonomous AI systems.

stories.title: Meta may use sweeping new commercial TOS to avoid millions in AI licensing fees
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Meta is reportedly updating its commercial Terms of Service (TOS).
The changes are seen by legal experts as a potential strategy to circumvent significant AI licensing costs.
The move is being framed as a major power consolidation play by Meta in the AI landscape.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its capability in conversational or creative AI applications.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, placing it within the current state-of-the-art LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in generative AI tasks.
The model is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: autotrust/JEV-27B-VL
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, autotrust/JEV-27B-VL, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model operates within the image-text-to-text pipeline, indicating multimodal capabilities.
It is associated with key technologies like transformers, safetensors, and the Qwen3.5 architecture.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and context gathering.
It is optimized to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing on-device AI capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 when running on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: Anthropic gives outside AI watchdog “employee-like” access
stories.author: Cristina Criddle, Financial Times
bullet_points: Anthropic is granting an external AI watchdog significant oversight capabilities.
The watchdog has the autonomy to publish its findings without requiring Anthropic's prior approval.
This signals a growing industry trend toward external accountability and governance in advanced AI development.

stories.title: Language Models Learn to Improve Language Models
stories.author: Hanqing Lu
bullet_points: LLMs are being used to automate AI research, specifically in language model development.
The concept of recursive self-improvement in AI is being explored through this self-improvement loop.
A major hurdle is the high computational cost of training models to effectively learn from experimental feedback.

stories.title: Self-Reflective Chain-of-Thought (SRCoT): Evidence-Based Text Generation via a Closed-Loop Retrieve--Reflect--Revise Pipeline on Edge LLMs
stories.author: Adrian Paschke
bullet_points: Introduces Self-Reflective Chain-of-Thought (SRCoT), a new architecture for LLMs.
SRCoT uses a closed-loop Retrieve--Reflect--Revise pipeline to ensure evidence-based text generation.
The system manages different knowledge types (state, memory, experience) using provenance-labeled stores and BM25 retrieval.

stories.title: MobileInject: Evaluating Reasoning-to-Action Security of MLLM-Based Mobile Agents under Cross-Modal Consistency Injection
stories.author: Caifeng Shan
bullet_points: MLLM-based mobile agents are advancing into autonomous systems capable of perceiving and acting within smartphone environments.
A novel security risk is identified: adversaries can manipulate these agents via 'cross-modal consistency injection' embedded in mobile content.
The research specifically addresses the gap in understanding prompt injection vulnerabilities when applied across different modalities in a mobile context.

stories.title: Language Models Learn to Improve Language Models
stories.author: Hanqing Lu
bullet_points: LLMs are being used to automate AI research, specifically in developing other language models.
This trend suggests a potential path toward recursive self-improvement in AI systems.
A major hurdle is the high cost of training models to effectively learn from experimental feedback, particularly via Reinforcement Learning.

stories.title: Self-Reflective Chain-of-Thought (SRCoT): Evidence-Based Text Generation via a Closed-Loop Retrieve--Reflect--Revise Pipeline on Edge LLMs
stories.author: Adrian Paschke
bullet_points: Introduces Self-Reflective Chain-of-Thought (SRCoT), a new architecture for LLMs.
SRCoT uses a closed-loop Retrieve--Reflect--Revise pipeline to ensure evidence-based text generation.
The system manages different knowledge types (state, memory, experience) using provenance-labeled stores and BM25 retrieval.

stories.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents: LLM agents that think in latent space, act through text
stories.author: allinonai
bullet_points: Introduction of 'Hybrid Reasoning Agents,' a new class of LLM agents.
These agents are designed to perform reasoning within a latent space before acting via text.
The project is open-sourced, available on GitHub and Hugging Face, indicating active research.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection has released its first open-weight model, Beam, on the Ollama platform.
Beam is specifically engineered for complex tasks such as software engineering, reasoning, and agentic workflows.
The model is currently available for free access through Ollama Cloud for a limited duration.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the use of local/cloud AI models for AI agents.
The integration allows these AI agents to run securely within Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses the need for safe and deployable AI agent environments.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of typed decisions.
Decision models can process text to provide probabilistic answers for yes/no questions, choices, and scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Lenovo’s fast, comfy SteamOS handheld is hundreds off
stories.author: Cameron Faulkner
bullet_points: Lenovo Legion Go S offers a strong alternative to the Steam Deck OLED.
It features hardware upgrades, including a larger 8-inch IPS screen (1080p/120Hz) and double the RAM/storage.
The device runs identical software to the Steam Deck but includes a unique design with two-stage triggers.

stories.title: “thegentlemanpervert” producing AI CSAM is a NJ prosecutor, say cops
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: A New Jersey deputy Attorney General was arrested after being flagged for producing AI-generated Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) on Discord.
The incident highlights the growing and serious misuse of generative AI technology for illegal and harmful content creation.
The case demonstrates the intersection of digital safety, law enforcement, and the ethical/legal challenges posed by advanced AI tools.

stories.title: US Rep proposes bill to give video game buyers "ownership," not "a license"
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: A US Representative has introduced legislation aimed at granting video game buyers true 'ownership' of their purchases.
The proposal seeks to move beyond the current model where consumers only hold a 'license' to use the game.
The path to implementation faces substantial technical and legislative challenges.

stories.title: Bug turns one of the biggest fears about Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses into reality
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: A significant privacy vulnerability was found in Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses.
The reported bug, which realized a major consumer fear, has since been patched.
Despite the fix, underlying privacy concerns regarding the device remain a topic of discussion.

stories.title: Robust Function Calling for LLM Agents Under Interface Drift
stories.author: Partha Sarathi Roy
bullet_points: Addresses 'interface drift,' a practical reliability issue where LLM tool interfaces change post-deployment even if tool logic is stable.
Proposes a lightweight, training-free repair layer to restore robustness in function-calling agents.
Focuses on improving the reliability of tool-augmented LLM agents without requiring expensive base model retraining.

stories.title: AgentOnto: Ontology-Guided LLM Agents for Enterprise Data Analytics
stories.author: Jingyuan Wang
bullet_points: AgentOnto is a new LLM agent designed specifically for complex enterprise data analytics.
It addresses the challenge of connecting analytical requests to scattered knowledge (databases, documents) by using an explicit ontology.
The ontology guides the agent's analysis, aiming to improve accuracy and enable reliable feedback incorporation.

stories.title: From Memory Hits to Answerable Evidence: Query-Conditioned Memory Compilation for Long-Term Agent Memory
stories.author: Tong Xu
bullet_points: Introduces MemCompile, a new framework for managing long-term memory in AI agents.
Addresses the limitation where existing systems pass raw or expanded memory units without proper context conditioning.
Focuses on 'query-conditioned evidence compilation' to ensure only answer-relevant evidence is presented to the agent.

stories.title: Designing for Imperfect Prompts: A Simulation-Based Evaluation of an LLM-Based Enterprise Data Assistant Using Knowledge Graphs
stories.author: Alexander Mädche
bullet_points: Addresses a critical real-world challenge: business users providing imperfect, domain-specific prompts to LLM-based enterprise data assistants.
Proposes a solution involving a semantic mediation layer to automatically resolve ambiguities and improve prompt understanding.
The research uses a Design Science approach, evaluating the system's performance in a practical setting (CFO unit data lake).

stories.title: Optimist Deep Research: An Iterative, State-Centric Agent for Autonomous Literature Research
stories.author: Gihan Panapitiya
bullet_points: Introduces 'Optimist Deep Research,' an open-source agent designed for autonomous literature research.
Addresses a limitation in current RAG systems by modeling research as an iterative, state-centric process rather than a single retrieval step.
The agent maintains an explicit, mutable research state, allowing the system to adapt as new subquestions and evidence are encountered during the research process.

stories.title: FlashReFocus: Interactive Image Refocusing in Seconds
stories.author: Chih-Chung Hsu
bullet_points: FlashReFocus addresses the computational bottleneck of interactive image refocusing by avoiding repeated large diffusion model runs.
The research distinguishes between two sub-problems: recovering the in-focus image (requiring a generative prior) and rendering blur.
The goal is to enable near-instantaneous, interactive changes to the focal plane and depth of field in captured photographs.

stories.title: How Finite-Rank Bottlenecks Shape the Low-Rank Adaptation Landscape
stories.author: Binh T. Nguyen
bullet_points: The paper addresses the lack of theoretical understanding behind the effectiveness of Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) for fine-tuning large models.
It proposes a novel analysis that avoids relying on the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) regime, which typically linearizes the network.
The core finding suggests that the loss function's behavior with respect to adapted weights provides a key insight into the low-rank adaptation landscape.

stories.title: Peak-Memory Schedules You Can Trust: Exact Realization, Certified Optimality, and the Limits of Recomputation for Inference
stories.author: Boris Sheludko
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical need for low activation memory during real-time inference on resource-constrained devices.
It identifies operator ordering as a key, latency-free lever for optimizing memory usage in ML models.
The research highlights the unreliability of current compiler-based deployment methods, showing performance degradation when optimizing operator order in PyTorch Inductor.

stories.title: Robust Function Calling for LLM Agents Under Interface Drift
stories.author: Partha Sarathi Roy
bullet_points: Addresses 'interface drift' in LLM agents, where tool descriptions change post-deployment despite stable tool functionality.
Proposes a lightweight, training-free repair layer to restore robustness in function-calling systems.
Focuses on practical reliability issues in tool-augmented LLM agents without requiring costly base model retraining.

stories.title: Annotrace: A Workbench for Step-Level Annotation of Agent Traces
stories.author: Bin Wu
bullet_points: Introduces Annotrace, a workbench designed to address the manual and inconsistent labeling of LLM agent execution traces.
It solves a gap where observability platforms lack structured labeling and text annotation tools lack execution context (steps, tool calls).
Annotrace supports multiple trace formats, including OpenTelemetry GenAI, LangSmith, and Langfuse, standardizing trace data.

stories.title: Verbalising Model's Computation for Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness Detection
stories.author: Hanqi Yan
bullet_points: Introduces VERITAS, a new method to verbalize a language model's internal computation during Chain-of-Thought (CoT) generation.
Addresses a limitation in current CoT verification methods by explaining *how* reasoning unfaithfulness develops, rather than just detecting it.
Utilizes layer-wise Jacobian projection to track the emergence and transfer of reasoning anchors across model layers.

stories.title: Reasoning Models Can Control Their Chains of Thought When They Tell Themselves To
stories.author: Yoav Goldberg
bullet_points: The paper investigates 'Chain-of-Thought (CoT) controllability,' which is the ability of reasoning models to control the properties of their internal reasoning steps.
Current evaluations show very low controllability across various models when prompted to follow specific CoT constraints.
The authors suggest this low controllability might stem from overly simplistic prompting methods rather than an inherent limitation of the models themselves.

stories.title: Ignored, Not Refused: What Low Prompt-Injection Success Rates Hide in Small Tool-Using Agents
stories.author: Farig Yousuf Sadeque
bullet_points: The research investigates indirect prompt injection (IPI) vulnerabilities in small, tool-using AI agents that process untrusted external content.
It challenges the standard security benchmark (Attack Success Rate - ASR) by showing that most failed injection attempts are simply ignored by the agents.
The study audits 33,000 trajectories across eleven open-weight agents, revealing that 76-80% of failed attacks are effectively ignored rather than being actively refused.
